sources.entry: HTTP Toolkit - HTTP Toolkit is a cross-platform tool to intercept, debug & mock HTTP.

summary.one_liner: HTTP Toolkit Desktop is the Electron-based build setup that packages the HTTP Toolkit UI and server into standalone installers for Windows, Linux and Mac.
summary.what_it_does: This repo builds a single desktop executable for HTTP Toolkit, a cross-platform HTTP(S) debugging proxy, analyzer and client. When the executable runs, it starts the httptoolkit-server (a node.js CLI application) in the background, opens the web UI in an Electron window, and kills the server when the window is closed. The repo itself contains only the Electron configuration, build setup and installer configuration, built with Electron Builder. Builds run on GitHub Actions, and tagged main builds are published as GitHub releases. The executable does not autoupdate; the server and web UI each handle their own updates. The UI and server can also be run separately, with the UI opened in any browser.
use_cases: Intercept and debug HTTP(S) traffic on desktop
Install a debugging proxy on Windows, Linux or Mac
Modify the desktop shell or add a new build target
notable: Bundles the httptoolkit-server and web UI into one desktop executable
Starts and stops the background server automatically with the app window
Builds installers for Windows, Linux and Mac via GitHub Actions
UI and server can be used separately, with the UI in any browser
caveats: The resulting executable does not autoupdate at the moment
This repo covers only the desktop shell; bugs in the UI or server belong to the main httptoolkit repository
